principles: Routine validation and DONE-required validation must remain separate surfaces.
Required DONE evidence must be mechanical, fresh, and hash-bound.
External projects must stay advisory unless they explicitly opt in.
Prompt/docs guidance is insufficient without runtime gate consumption.
drivers: B-3321 verified that configured validate.commands can be narrower than root npm test.
DONE output must not overclaim full-suite assurance.
Self-host needs stricter assurance than default external projects.

options.name: A: Top-level doneRequiredCommands plus separate done-required-evidence.json and done_required_validate command
pros: DONE oracle can consume a distinct artifact
Self-host opt-in is explicit and external defaults remain advisory
Smoke tests can exercise the runner with fake commands
cons: Adds a new CLI command and artifact type

options.name: B: validationProfiles.done plus profile-aware validate command
cons: Higher risk of confusing routine validate with DONE-required proof
More migration/documentation work for this story

options.name: C: Append root npm test to validate.commands
cons: Rejected by B-3321 as the final solution
Does not create a distinct DONE-required assurance claim
Does not keep external opt-in semantics clean

chosen: A: Top-level doneRequiredCommands plus separate done-required-evidence.json and done_required_validate command
rationale: Choose A because it creates an explicit DONE-required evidence path without changing routine validate behavior. It is the smallest runtime implementation that satisfies B-3321 gate semantics, freshness, self-host opt-in, and external advisory defaults.

preMortem.scenario: DONE blocks every external project after upgrade
preMortem.trigger: The oracle treats missing doneRequiredCommands as failure instead of advisory
preMortem.consequence: Lattice becomes too expensive and breaks non-self-host users
preMortem.mitigation: Gate fails only when a required policy is configured; missing policy renders advisory/pass row with no full-suite claim.

preMortem.scenario: Stale root npm test receipt satisfies DONE
preMortem.consequence: DONE still overclaims assurance after code or policy changes
preMortem.mitigation: Artifact records headHash, materialHash, storyFilesHash, policyHash, and commandSetHash; oracle rejects mismatch with explicit stale reason.

preMortem.scenario: Root npm test runs against stale packages/main/dist
preMortem.trigger: The root test command is recorded without a same-material build receipt
preMortem.consequence: Full-suite evidence is false because built CLI output does not match source
preMortem.mitigation: Self-host required policy demands an earlier build receipt or equivalent same-material build proof before root npm test can pass.

preMortem.scenario: The change becomes prose-only process policy
preMortem.trigger: Process fact registry and verifier are not updated
preMortem.consequence: Future refactors can remove the gate artifact without failing tests
preMortem.mitigation: Register done_required_validate and done-required-evidence in process-fact registry, levels, and verify-process-fact-contract.mjs.

preMortem.scenario: The story expands into release/pre-push/Authority production work
preMortem.trigger: M8 future alignment language is implemented in this story
preMortem.consequence: Scope grows beyond the user-confirmed implementation and increases risk
preMortem.mitigation: Scope boundary excludes release_approve_push, pre-push behavior, Authority receipts, Layer4, customerKeyRef, and emergency override implementation.
